$schema: the adversarial op-plan inputs core/opplan is proven against (llm-contract.md §1): each case is `input` (the reply text, verbatim), `parts` ([chunk, times] pairs concatenated) or `inputBase64` (raw bytes, WHATWG-decoded); `expect` is the verdict the JS reference decides, checked by npm run gen-fixtures

cases.name: oracle-proto-op-names
cases.note: op names that are Object.prototype members are unknown ops: a warning each, never a lookup through the prototype

cases.name: oracle-proto-key-constructor
cases.note: "constructor" is an unknown field

cases.name: oracle-proto-key-dunder
cases.note: "__proto__" is an own, unknown field after JSON.parse

cases.name: oracle-proto-key-top-level
cases.note: an unknown top-level key is ignored, "__proto__" too: its actions never run

cases.name: oracle-proto-regexby-axis
cases.note: an axis named like a prototype member fails its enum, never selects a grammar

cases.name: oracle-dup-reply-last-wins
cases.note: a duplicate key keeps its last value

cases.name: oracle-dup-op-last-wins
cases.note: the last "op" decides the action

cases.name: oracle-dup-bad-then-good
cases.note: an invalid value overwritten by a valid one is never seen

cases.name: oracle-dup-key-first-position
cases.note: a duplicate keeps its FIRST position: "zz" is reported, not "yy"

cases.name: oracle-int-keys-ascending
cases.note: integer-like keys come first, ascending (JS Object.keys): "9" is the first unknown field

cases.name: oracle-int-keys-index-edge
cases.note: 4294967294 is an array index and comes first; 4294967295 is not one and keeps insertion order

cases.name: oracle-int-keys-not-canonical
cases.note: "01" and "-1" are strings, "1" is an index

cases.name: oracle-num-1e400
cases.note: 1e400 parses to Infinity, which is not an integer

cases.name: oracle-num-1e-400
cases.note: 1e-400 underflows to 0, below the 0.1 cm floor

cases.name: oracle-num-2.0
cases.note: 2.0 is the integer 2 and comes back as 2

cases.name: oracle-num-minus-zero
cases.note: -0 is >= 0 for the frame index but below 1 for times

cases.name: oracle-num-minus-zero-frame
cases.note: -0 passes as 0 and is written back as 0

cases.name: oracle-num-near-integer
cases.note: the first rounds to 3; the second is not an integer

cases.name: oracle-num-echo
cases.note: layout numbers come back in JS String() form

cases.name: oracle-astral-at-cap
cases.note: 60 astral characters are 120 UTF-16 units: exactly the save-name cap

cases.name: oracle-astral-over-cap
cases.note: 121 units: over the cap

cases.name: oracle-lone-surrogates-at-cap
cases.note: 120 escaped lone surrogates are 120 units; each comes back as U+FFFD

cases.name: oracle-lone-surrogates-over-cap
cases.note: 121 units: over the cap

cases.name: oracle-escaped-pair-is-one-char
cases.note: an escaped surrogate PAIR is one astral character; the lone halves in the reply become U+FFFD

cases.name: oracle-lone-surrogate-op-name
cases.note: the warning names the op with U+FFFD for the lone surrogate

cases.name: oracle-trim-nbsp-reply
cases.note: NBSP and U+3000 are JS whitespace: the reply is omitted, so "Done." plus a warning

cases.name: oracle-trim-set-url
cases.note: the url is trimmed with the JS WhiteSpace + LineTerminator set

cases.name: oracle-trim-not-zwsp
cases.note: U+200B is not whitespace: the url does not start with http

cases.name: oracle-trim-not-nel-mvs
cases.note: U+0085 and U+180E are not JS whitespace, so the server is not blank

cases.name: oracle-trim-line-sep-blank
cases.note: line and paragraph separators, VT and FF are whitespace: the server is blank

cases.name: oracle-trim-chat-only
cases.note: a chat-only reply is trimmed with the same set

cases.name: oracle-trim-ask-question
cases.note: trimmed ask text comes back without the Unicode spaces

cases.name: oracle-digits-arabic-crop
cases.note: the crop grammar's digits are ASCII only

cases.name: oracle-digits-fullwidth-page
cases.note: a fullwidth digit is not a page size

cases.name: oracle-digits-fullwidth-formula
cases.note: a fullwidth digit is outside the formula charset

cases.name: oracle-digits-arabic-aspect
cases.note: nor an aspect

cases.name: oracle-bom-before-object
cases.note: a BOM before the object is prose around it

cases.name: oracle-bom-inside-object
cases.note: a BOM is not JSON whitespace: the object does not parse, so the turn is chat-only

cases.name: oracle-broken-then-good
cases.note: only the FIRST balanced object is tried: it does not parse, so the turn is chat-only

cases.name: oracle-brace-in-string-then-good
cases.note: the scanner is string-aware; the first object has no reply, so the plan is empty

cases.name: oracle-unbalanced
cases.note: no balanced object: chat-only

cases.name: oracle-fenced
cases.note: fences and their language tag are stripped

cases.name: oracle-leading-zero
cases.note: a leading zero is not JSON: chat-only

cases.name: oracle-trailing-comma
cases.note: a trailing comma is not JSON: chat-only

cases.name: oracle-raw-control-char
cases.note: a raw tab inside a string is not JSON: chat-only

cases.name: oracle-escapes-echo
cases.note: escapes decode, and the reply is written back with JSON.stringify escaping

cases.name: oracle-nest-64
cases.note: 64 levels (the root object is 1) is the cap

cases.name: oracle-nest-65
cases.note: one level deeper fails the plan: E_JSON_LIMIT

cases.name: oracle-nest-10k
cases.note: 10k levels is still valid JSON: the cap fails it, and nothing recurses

cases.name: oracle-nest-10k-broken
cases.note: 10k levels that never close: the object is unbalanced, so chat-only

cases.name: oracle-nest-10k-bad-syntax
cases.note: balanced but not JSON: chat-only, never a limit error

cases.name: oracle-nodes-at-cap
cases.note: 262144 values (root, reply, array, 262141 zeros) is the cap

cases.name: oracle-nodes-over-cap
cases.note: one value more: E_JSON_LIMIT

cases.name: oracle-bytes-at-cap
cases.note: the object is exactly 2 MiB

cases.name: oracle-bytes-over-cap
cases.note: one byte more: E_JSON_LIMIT

cases.name: oracle-bytes-multibyte-over
cases.note: bytes are UTF-8 bytes, not characters: 2-byte letters cross the cap

cases.name: oracle-rule-message-dollar
cases.note: a surface rule quotes the value verbatim ("$&" is no replacement pattern); the cli refuses the path, the desktop the colour

cases.name: oracle-utf8-lone-continuation
cases.note: a stray continuation byte is U+FFFD

cases.name: oracle-utf8-overlong
cases.note: an overlong encoding is two U+FFFD

cases.name: oracle-utf8-truncated
cases.note: a truncated sequence is ONE U+FFFD (its maximal subpart)

cases.name: oracle-utf8-cesu-surrogate
cases.note: an encoded surrogate is three U+FFFD

cases.name: oracle-utf8-above-max
cases.note: above U+10FFFF, and 0xFF

cases.name: oracle-utf8-in-save-name-cap
cases.note: 120 bad bytes are 120 U+FFFD: exactly the cap

cases.name: oracle-utf8-outside-object
cases.note: malformed bytes around the object are prose

cases.name: oracle-utf8-chat-only
cases.note: a chat-only reply keeps its U+FFFD
